title: Data Solutions routing descriptor
doc: The ONE reviewed source for where a Data Solutions operation goes.
Everything downstream is generated from this file:
* the public, build-time routes manifest the browser/desktop bundle loads
(scripts/routing/generate-routes.mjs, one file per target);
* the contract test that proves each declared gateway path really exists
in ds-apis-tf and really points at the backend declared here.
Two hard rules, enforced by the generator and by tests:
1. `backend` / `relays_to` name PRIVATE Cloud Run services. They are
reviewed here and validated against the IaC; they are NEVER copied
into the generated public manifest. The browser learns one origin:
the lane's EDS API Gateway (or its own origin in local development).
2. A retired service may never appear. ds-solar-calc and ds-solar-reporter
are retired; Python is out of the application stack except for
ds-solar-weather, which is private and reached only by ds-brain.
The reviewed default for every field of the operation registry
(ds-command-kernel/docs/contracts/ds-transport-authority.md section 3).
An operation that omits a field inherits the value declared HERE. That
keeps the default a reviewed line in the descriptor rather than a constant
buried in the generator, and it lets an entry that is genuinely ordinary
stay short. Any entry may override any field.
`principal` says which credential the call carries, and only that:
* `user`      — a Firebase user bearer is attached;
* `anonymous` — NO DS user bearer is ever attached. The platform API key
is still sent (the gateway requires it) and a device credential may be
the real principal. Attaching a bearer to an `anonymous` operation
silently widens its read scope, so the client refuses to.
`authority` says which origin answers:
* `gateway`         — this build's own lane EDS API Gateway;
* `release`         — the public release authority, which may cross lanes;
* `storage_session` — a DS-minted storage session URI is the WHOLE
credential: no Authorization, no api key, no user email. No operation
declares it yet; the value exists so the transfer slice can.

ds_brain_bulk_url.note: Existing bulk execution lane of ds-brain, including the protected media route.

ds_brain_url.note: The only backend the public gateway routes browser traffic to.

ds_solar_weather_url.note: The sole sanctioned Python service. Reached ONLY as a bounded ds-brain relay; it has no gateway surface of its own.

ds_solar_engine_url.note: The Cloud Run adapter over the same Rust runtime linked into the installed application. Reached only through ds-brain.

ds_network_reporter_url.note: Report worker. ds-brain orchestrates it; the browser never addresses it.

web-canary.summary: web + canary — Firebase Hosting against the canary EDS API Gateway

web-production.summary: web + production — Firebase Hosting against the production EDS API Gateway

desktop-production.summary: desktop production release — packaged installer against the production gateway

printing.summary: Shared global and project print layouts; GeoJSON vector delivery.

architecture.summary: Governed platform architecture planning and revision authority.

planning.summary: Read, preview, apply, and inspect governed architecture revisions.

solar.summary: Solar control plane. The same Rust runtime executes locally in the installed app and behind Cloud Run for the web.

portfolio.list.summary: List governed Solar portfolios and their exact ordered membership.

data.read_input.summary: Read one city's authored Solar input record.

data.save_input.summary: Create or update one city's Solar input record.

seed.preview.summary: Plan, without mutating, what seeding a project's Solar root from the governed seed source would do.
doc: Read-only. ds-brain returns the exact cities, input documents and
network assets that WOULD be seeded, plus the seed_digest that binds
the plan to its apply.
Both placements resolve to the gateway on purpose: ds-brain is the
only Firestore authority and the installed engine holds no GCP
credential (SOLAR_CONTRACTS section 6). The door is still selected
explicitly so no feature module infers placement for itself.

seed.apply.summary: Apply exactly the previewed Solar seed plan, confirmed by its digest.
doc: Idempotent and digest-bound. The caller echoes the seed_digest of the
plan it previewed; ds-brain re-plans and refuses on any drift.

data.locality.summary: Solar data-locality configuration (which Firestore root a project reads).

reference_unit.summary: Seal one city's reference PV unit and return its artifact inventory.
doc: gateway -> ds-brain -> ds-solar-weather. ds-brain adds Cloud Run service
identity and relays a closed request; the response is an inventory of
signed URLs. This is the ONLY route in the product that ends at Python,
and it is a reference unit, never a calculation.
Web: gateway -> ds-brain -> private Rust ds-solar Cloud Run adapter.
Desktop: the linked Rust runtime through the native command.
Both publish the same project result contract; placement is not result identity.

compute_batch.summary: Calculate a selected set of cities as one closed batch.

desktop_snapshot.summary: The installed native client's bounded Solar project snapshot.
doc: Fetched by ds-client-core inside the installed application, never by
the application bundle, so both placements close it here while the
Rust registry still carries the row.

unavailable_reason.web: The desktop snapshot is a native-client read; the browser reads Solar through the ordinary solar operations.
unavailable_reason.desktop: The desktop snapshot is fetched by the installed native client, not by the application bundle.

report.generate.summary: Produce the calculation-backed APD for a city.

unavailable_reason.web: Solar document production is desktop-native. The retired Python ds-solar-reporter service must never be used.

report.summary: Run a network report or export through the ds-brain pipeline door.

design_collaboration.summary: Governed selections, attachments, annotations, tags and comment threads for design objects.
doc: `selections.actions` is exactly the closed vocabulary the native client
may send (ds-client-core DESIGN_SELECTIONS_ACTIONS), declared so a saved
Transformer Status selection is readable and assignable headlessly; it
bumped the client profile schema to v20. The browser lane sends three
further selection actions - describe_query, list_assignments and update -
which are NOT declared: the first two are browser surfaces and the third
renames a selection without touching membership. Declaring them is a
descriptor edit plus a review, not a code change. Attachments and
annotations stay browser-only operations and declare no vocabulary.

selections.summary: Read and mutate named transformer selections.

attachments.summary: Read and mutate immutable design attachment revisions.

annotations.summary: Read and mutate typed design tags and comment threads.

versions.summary: Read and create metadata-only design object versions without transporting geometry.

assets.summary: Project Assets: the catalogue of documents a project holds, in folders, with previews, classification, links and audited reads.

action.summary: One action-multiplexed call on the project assets catalogue: list, tree, get, download, grant, audit_list, folder_create, folder_update, classify, attach, detach, ingest_start, ingest_finalize.
doc: ds-web/docs/project-assets-contract.md (D21): one POST endpoint, `ds_project` + `action`, DisallowUnknownFields,
64 KiB body. Reads are membership-only and keep working on archived projects; writes are lifecycle-gated and
capability-resolved against the body's project. ds-brain is the only authority on redaction (§6.2) and it never
stores a download_url (§12.11). The gateway declaration is Appendix A of the contract and lands in ds-apis-tf.

auth.summary: Authenticated Desktop identity handoff. Device credential creation remains native-client-owned.

device.approve.summary: Approve or deny one pending device authorization as the signed-in Firebase principal.
doc: This is the only device-authorization operation owned by the Desktop UI.
It accepts no requested principal, project, token, private key or device proof.
Headless begin, status, complete, refresh and inventory operations are not Desktop bridge operations.

device.begin.summary: Start one device authorization from a device proof.
doc: Native-client operation. It is declared so the ONE registry describes
the whole device-credential lifecycle the Rust client speaks; the
application bundle never performs it and the manifest closes it on
both placements.

unavailable_reason.web: Device credential creation is owned by the native client; the browser bundle performs only domains.auth.device.approve.
unavailable_reason.desktop: Device credential creation is owned by the native client, not by the application bundle; the Desktop UI performs only domains.auth.device.approve.

doc: `principal: anonymous` means only that NO Firebase user bearer is
attached. The device credential signature is the real principal.

messaging.summary: Messaging commands, attachments and the account/conversation streams. All mounted on ds-brain; there is no separate messaging origin in any lane.

desktop_manifest.summary: Latest published desktop release for a channel.
doc: The ONLY operation that may address an origin other than this build's
own lane gateway: the public download page must be able to offer the
canary installer from a production build, and the canary app must
never read stable's release document. Both authorities are EDS API
Gateways; neither may be a private run.app service.

grid.summary: DS Grid global catalogue, project models, and the anonymous public example reads.
doc: All three were direct gateway bypasses until 2026-09-10: they built their
own Authorization / x-api-key headers, carried no X-Request-Id or
X-DS-Action-Id, and appeared in no descriptor. They are declared here so
the ONE client can carry them.

catalog.action.summary: Governed global library/example inventory and publisher actions.

models.action.summary: Membership-gated project DS Grid model heads, immutable revisions and exports.
doc: `start_upload` returns a resumable session URI. The session is an
`authority: storage_session` transfer that the caller never sees; it
does not re-enter this operation.

examples.list.summary: List the anonymously visible public DS Grid example heads.
doc: Deliberately anonymous. Public example reads must keep working
signed-out; a user bearer would silently widen the visibility scope
and make "works signed-out" untestable.

examples.get.summary: Resolve one public example revision and its short-lived signed model URL.
doc: Anonymous, like examples.list. The signed URL is transport only:
trust comes from the revision digest, verified in the browser.

heartbeat.summary: Register the exact native installation and return its signed lease.

work.summary: Signed native work admission and publication declaration.

open.summary: Open one installation- and project-fenced native work grant.

publish.summary: Declare one grant-fenced native publication after its exact transfers.

compute_artifacts.summary: Durable local-first artifact publication: open, transfer, finalize, discover.
doc: The JSON control plane only. The bytes move over the resumable-transfer
protocol (contract section 4), whose session URI is an
`authority: storage_session` credential this endpoint mints and never
returns to a feature module.

open.summary: Bind an immutable client run and return upload sessions or existing generations.

status.summary: Recover durable publication work after a restart.

finalize.summary: Verify exact bytes and advance the operation/variant head behind its fences.
doc: A digest or length mismatch is a terminal conflict, never a retry
loop (contract section 4.2 rule 8), so retry_class stays
transport_only.

read.summary: Read one current head's safe output metadata.

download.summary: Mint a short-lived read URL from a server-recorded output id and generation.
doc: The caller never supplies a storage path. The minted URL is itself an
`authority: storage_session` read and carries no DS credential.
Observability only: it must never affect UX, so it declares no retry
and a short deadline. ds-brain mounts it with OPTIONAL authentication
on purpose — pre-login boot crashes are the most valuable events — so
the platform key is the access guard and the bearer is a bonus.

survey_entries.summary: Governed Survey entry creation with a verified commit receipt.

create.summary: Create one exact survey entry or replay its stable idempotency key.

survey_media.summary: Governed exact-path survey media upload and conditional replacement.

action.summary: Inspect a pinned source, issue an upload session, or verify uploaded bytes.

project_data.summary: Project data-file inventory and upload lifecycle.

action.summary: List, start an upload, upload, or delete one project data file.

status_processing.summary: Standard design-intake upload and one-file processing.

action.summary: Issue an upload session or process one uploaded LV design file.
Read one shared class style, seed a starter style without persisting it, or assemble one work-map runtime family.

update.summary: Apply one reviewed style instruction to a project layer.

layers.summary: The assembled layer document, the Style Center catalogue and governed project presentation defaults.

action.summary: Read the project's assembled layer document or style catalogue, or save canonical order and starting-visibility overrides.

tiles.summary: Project vector-tile status, generation and catalogue.

action.summary: Inspect, preflight, generate or curate a project's tiles.

project_forms.summary: Which survey forms a project has active, and their settings.

action.summary: Activate forms, read/write the settings editor, or bulk-save.

project_report.summary: The compounded project deliverable, the transformer inventory, and the status rows behind it.
doc: `actions` is exactly the closed vocabulary the native client may send
(ds-client-core PROJECT_REPORT_ACTIONS). list_transformers_status was
declared for the headless Design read spine and bumped the client
profile schema to v19. The browser lane sends four further /report
actions — add_transfo_to_combined, combined_and_export,
export_reports_only, refresh_mv_reports — which are NOT declared yet.
Declaring them is a descriptor edit plus a review, not a code change.

action.summary: Compounded deliverable, archive registry, inventory, retirement, status rows.

data_distribution.summary: The governed geographic dataset catalogue and the derived print context ds-brain relays to the vector tiler.
doc: `actions` is exactly the closed vocabulary the native client may send
(ds-client-core DATA_DISTRIBUTION_ACTIONS): the catalogue read a headless
seeder plans national-bundle installs from, and the bounded buildings /
contours acquisition behind first-print seeding. Declaring it bumped the
client profile schema to v21. The browser lane also sends query_dataset
(billed BigQuery pages) and the publication actions discover_datasets,
reconcile_datasets, publish_dataset and publication_status, which are NOT
declared: a headless caller never falls back to a billed page query, and
publication is an operator surface. Declaring them is a descriptor edit
plus a review, not a code change. The bundle a catalogue row names is
fetched from storage.googleapis.com without any DS credential; that is
not a gateway operation and is pinned in ds-client-core.

action.summary: List the project's catalogue rows, or acquire one bounded derived print context.

admin_bounds.summary: The national administrative hierarchy: exact immediate children, and one unit's polygon.
doc: The country is a PATH segment, not a parameter: `/api/v1/admin/rwanda`
is Rwanda's authority and a second country is a second reviewed route.
`actions` is exactly the closed vocabulary the native client may send
(ds-client-core ADMIN_BOUNDS_ACTIONS). Declaring it bumped the client
profile schema to v28.
The backend (ds-brain `internal/bulk/handlers/admin_handler.go`) also
answers `hierarchy`, `descendants`, `query`, `locate` and a POST
`enrich`. None is declared: `descendants` pulls every unit of a level
WITH geometry in one unbounded answer, `hierarchy` and `query` say what
`children` and `geometry` already say exactly, and `locate` and `enrich`
are spatial joins a caller performs against the installed reference
asset. `geometry` and `wkt` are backend aliases for the same GeoJSON
read; this client sends the one that means it.
ds-apis-tf declares the `action` query parameter with an enum that
predates `geometry` and `descendants`. The gateway does not enforce it
-- ds-web has read `action=geometry` in production since Search place
shipped -- but the enum is stale and worth correcting there.

action.summary: List one level's exact immediate children, or read one boundary's geometry.
